done.changed: Local Qwen dev authored improve/metacheck.py from a precise PM spec and passed the objective fixture verify on attempt 2/3. The pure, stdlib-only audit_meta(out_dir, max_title_chars=60, max_desc_chars=155) mirrors the canonicalcheck/linkcheck audit style: walk docs/**/*.html, page id = relpath (forward slashes), read UTF-8, use re + html.unescape. For each page it counts <title> tags and <meta name="description" content=...> tags and returns a list of problem dicts {page,kind,severity,detail}. STRUCTURAL errors (severity='error', fail the build): missing_title / multiple_title (0 or >1 <title>), missing_description / multiple_description. The objective verify (/tmp/verify_meta.py) builds a temp docs tree exercising every kind plus two fully-clean pages and asserts audit_meta returns EXACTLY the expected 12 (page,kind) problems with the right severity per kind and zero false positives on the clean pages. PM wired exactly two things into build.py (mirroring the canonical gate): load metacheck.py by path, and after the canonical audit run audit_meta(OUT) as a post-build gate that always prints the warnings, prints+fails (SystemExit 1) on any severity='error', and otherwise prints an OK line with the warning count. done.title: DEPTH: build-time canonical audit — assert every rendered page's rel=canonical exactly equals its own BASE_URL page URL (never root-relative, never pointing at another page), a build.py post-build check that fails the build on drift, so canonicalization can never silently regress.
done.changed: Local Qwen dev authored improve/canonicalcheck.py from a precise PM spec and passed the objective fixture verify on attempt 1/3. The pure, stdlib-only audit_canonicals(out_dir, base_url) walks docs/**/*.html and, for each page, computes the EXPECTED self-referential canonical from its own on-disk path: a directory index (index.html) -> BASE_URL + '/<dir>/' (root index -> BASE_URL + '/'), and a literal file (e.g. 404.html) -> BASE_URL + '/404.html' — an edge case the PM verified in the real output, where docs/404.html carries a literal-file canonical, not a directory-index one. It extracts every <link ... rel=canonical ...> tag (robust to attribute order + single/double quotes), html-unescapes the href, and returns a problem dict {page,kind,detail} for kind='missing' (0 canonical tags), 'duplicate' (>1), or 'mismatch' (the single href != the computed self URL); returns [] when clean. The objective verify (/tmp/verify_canonical.py) builds a temp docs tree with correct root/dir/nested/404 canonicals plus one drifted, one missing, and one duplicated page and asserts the function flags EXACTLY those three with the right kinds and zero false positives on the correct pages. PM wired exactly two things into build.py (mirroring the linkcheck.py gate): load canonicalcheck.py by path, and after the existing internal-link audit run audit_canonicals(OUT, BASE_URL) as a post-build gate that prints a per-problem report and raise SystemExit(1) on any drift. Validated: build GREEN (11 guide pages + 2 posts); canonical audit reports 0 problems across the real site; full SEO gate GREEN on index (one <title>, one meta description, one rel=canonical, JSON-LD Article, exactly one <h1>, sitemap.xml present) and a single-<h1> + JSON-LD-parse sweep is CLEAN across all 16 output pages. done.title: FIX (internal links): in-body markdown links authored root-relative (/slug/) 404'd on the GitHub Pages project subpath — prefix them with BASE_URL
done.changed: Fixed a live sitewide SEO defect. Markdown body links were authored root-relative (e.g. [read this](/content-quality/)) and build.py's inline() renderer passed the href through verbatim, so on the project-subpath deploy (https://connor-enge.github.io/seo-guide/, with NO <base> tag) all 53 in-body internal links across 12 pages resolved to https://connor-enge.github.io/<slug>/ and 404'd — bleeding internal link equity and dead-ending both crawlers and readers. (Nav/header/footer/related/pager links were already correct because they are built with page_url()/BASE_URL; only the hand-written in-prose links were broken.) Local Qwen dev authored improve/links.py — a pure, stdlib-only resolve_href(href, base_url) that prefixes single-'/'-rooted hrefs with base_url and leaves fragments (#…), absolute/external (http(s)://, //), mailto:/tel:/javascript:/data:, empty, and already-relative hrefs untouched; idempotent and never double-prefixes an already-absolute href — self-corrected against an objective 16-case verify (root-relative→prefixed; fragment/external/protocol-relative/mailto/tel/empty/base-absolute untouched; idempotent; trailing-slash base tolerated). PM wired exactly two things in build.py: load the helper by path (mirroring the breadcrumb/anchors/notfound helpers) and route inline()'s [text](href) substitution through resolve_href(href, BASE_URL) via a lambda. Validated: build green (11 guide pages + 2 posts); root-relative body links sitewide went 53 -> 0; the fixed links now carry the full BASE_URL (verified on glossary/index + others); every #fragment anchor still intact; full SEO gate GREEN on index (title/description/canonical/JSON-LD Article/exactly one <h1>/sitemap present); and a single-<h1> + JSON-LD-parse sweep is clean across all 14 output pages.
